html:
The Marksville culture was a Native American culture of the lower Mississippi Valley, mainly in Louisiana and Mississippi, from about 100 BCE to 400 CE. It was the southern part of the Hopewell world: its people built burial mounds and shared Hopewell styles of pottery, figurines, copper and stone pipes.

It is named after the Marksville site in Louisiana, a group of mounds inside a half-circle earth wall. People there lived by hunting, fishing and gathering, and grew some local plants.

It followed the much older Poverty Point tradition of the same region. Its neighbours were the Fourche Maline culture to the west and the Swift Creek culture to the east. Later cultures of the lower Mississippi grew out of it and led toward the mound towns of the Mississippian era.
